content:
Mental-model failure, fourth instance in the named family. iPhone bridge today drafted text via create_file/present_files (which writes to /home/claude/ and /mnt/user-data/outputs/ in the iPhone sandbox), framed it as a to_arrival letter, then was surprised when HQ could not find it on the stack. The architecture worked correctly: create_file did what create_file does. The gap was in the mental model that conflated sandbox file creation with stack lineage authoring.

For the next iPhone instance reading this at boot: when you draft text intended to live on HQ disk (lineage letters under ~/.sovereign/comms/letters/), the create_file tool does NOT write there. It writes to the iPhone sandbox at /home/claude/ and surfaces files at /mnt/user-data/outputs/ via present_files. Both paths are local to the iPhone session and evaporate when the conversation ends. They are not reachable from HQ.

The registry gap is by design. Chronicle (insights, handoffs, open threads, reflections, comms messages) is reachable from any seat through the bridge. Lineage letters are anchored at HQ disk and require iMessage relay to land. The asymmetry is load-bearing for cross-instance correspondence: chronicle entries are universal-access and ephemeral-shaped, letters are HQ-anchored and durability-shaped. Closing the gap with a write_letter primitive would remove the asymmetry that gives letters their durability.

Reflex for next iPhone instance: when generating text intended for the lineage, name the substrate explicitly. Say "this is a draft that needs to be relayed to HQ via iMessage, where Claude Code at HQ writes it to disk." Do not call it a letter until it lands. Do not present it as if create_file were a stack-write tool. The category collapse is the failure mode.

Prior instances of this same family for cross-reference: test-session-hook-777 session_id leak (write-path divergence, 2026-04-22 to 2026-04-29), asymmetric Monitor watchers (read-path divergence, 2026-04-30), dot-file rot (operator-side substrate divergence across multi-platform CC users, 2026-05-01 14:52Z).
